blocks:
The explanation of the word of Allah — exalted is His praise, hallowed are His names: الْقَارِعَةُ (1)

Allah — exalted is His remembrance — says: al-Qāriʿa (the Striker): the Hour that strikes the hearts of people with its terror and with the tremendous affliction (balāʾ) that befalls them thereby. That is the morning after which no night follows.

In accordance with what we have said about this, the exegetes of the Qurʾān (ahl al-taʾwīl) likewise spoke.

* Mention of who said that.

ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, on the authority of ʿAlī, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the word al-Qāriʿa : it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection (yawm al-qiyāma); Allah has exalted it and has warned His servants of it.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the word الْقَارِعَةُ * مَا الْقَارِعَةُ — he said: that is the Hour (al-Sāʿa).

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning His word الْقَارِعَةُ * مَا الْقَارِعَةُ — he said: that is the Hour.

Abū Kurayb related to us, saying: Wakīʿ related to us, saying: I heard that al-Qāriʿa, al-Wāqiʿa, and al-Ḥāqqa all three mean the Resurrection (al-qiyāma).

And His word: مَا الْقَارِعَةُ (What is the Striking Calamity?) — the Exalted, whose praise is glorified, says this in order to magnify the gravity of the Resurrection and the Hour, whereby the servants are struck with dread of it: 'What is the Striking Calamity?' — that is to say: what is the Hour that strikes the creation through dread of it? That is to say: how tremendous, how dreadful, and how awe-inspiring it is.

And His statement: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ (And what made you know what the Striking Calamity is?) — Here the Exalted — praise be to Him — says to His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: What made you realize, O Muḥammad, what the Striking Calamity (al-qāriʿah) is?

And His word: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ (the day on which mankind will be like scattered moths): the Exalted — magnified be His mention — says: the Striking Calamity is the day on which mankind will be like the farāsh — that is the insect that falls into the fire and the lamp; it is neither a mosquito nor a fly — and by al-mabthūth He means: the scattered, the dispersed.

In accordance with what we have said about this, the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwīl) have also spoken.

* Mention of who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ : "These are the farāsh that you have seen plunging into the fire."

Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His word يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ : "This is a parable that Allah has set forth." And some of the Arabic philologists (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) said: the meaning of this is: like a swarm of locusts, crawling over one another; thus are mankind on that day — they teem in confusion over one another.

His statement: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ — Allah, exalted be His remembrance, says: and on the day that the mountains will be like carded wool; and al-ʿihn is multicolored wool.

In accordance with what we have said about this, the people of interpretation also spoke.

* Mention of who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning His statement: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ — he said: carded wool.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of Qatāda, who said: it is the wool. And it was mentioned that the mountains move along over the earth while they still have the form of mountains, like dust.

And His word: فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ (As for him whose scales are heavy) — He says: as for him whose scales of good deeds are heavy. By "the scales" (mawāzīn) He means: the weight. The Arabs say: "With me you have a dirham equal to the scale (mīzān) of your dirham" and "equal to the weight of your dirham," and they say: "My house is equal to the scale (mīzān) of your house and the weight of your house" — by which is meant: opposite your house. The poet has said:

Before our meeting I was a man of strength,
with every adversary I had his scale (mīzān) at hand.

By his words "with every adversary his scale" he means: his word with which he refutes the argument of the adversary. And Mujāhid used to say: "There is no scale — it is only a likeness that is set forth."

Abū Kurayb related this to us, saying: Wakīʿ related to us, on the authority of Sufyān, on the authority of Ibn Abī Najīḥ, on the authority of Mujāhid, concerning فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ: he said: 'in a life that he finds pleasing, in the Garden (janna).'

Likewise, Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ: he means: in the Garden (janna).

His word: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ — "And as for him whose scales are light, his refuge is the Hāwiya" — He says: as for him whose scale of good deeds turns out light, his refuge and dwelling place is the Hāwiya, in which he falls upon his head into the Fire (jahannam).

In a manner similar to what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) have spoken.

* Mention of who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ : "It is the Fire — that is their refuge."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ ("then his mother is the Hāwiya"): he said: "His abode is the Fire — that is the Hāwiya." Qatāda said: "It is an Arabic expression; when a man fell into a grave matter, they would say: 'his mother has mourned' (hawat ummuhu)."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Maʿmar, on the authority of al-Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Aʿmā, who said: "When a believer dies, his soul is brought to the souls of the believers. Then they say: 'Give your brother rest, for he was in the tribulation of the world.' He said: And they ask him: 'What has so-and-so done?' Then he answers: 'He has died — or has he not yet arrived among you?' Then they say: 'He has been taken away to his mother, the Hāwiya.'"

Ismāʿīl ibn Sayf al-ʿIjlī related to me, saying: ʿAlī ibn Mushhir related to us, saying: Ismāʿīl related to us, on the authority of Abū Ṣāliḥ, concerning His word فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ: he said: "They plunge down into the Fire upon their heads."

Ibn Sayf related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sawwār related to us, on the authority of Saʿīd, on the authority of Qatāda, concerning فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ: he said: "He plunges down into the Fire upon his head."

Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His word فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ: "The Hāwiya is the Fire — it is his mother and his dwelling place to which he returns and in which he seeks shelter." And he recited: وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ ("and their dwelling place is the Fire").

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ: "And that is the likeness of it. The Fire was called his mother only because it has become his dwelling place, just as a woman gives shelter to her child. So the Fire, for him — now that he has no dwelling place other than it — is set in the position of a mother to him."

And His word: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ (And what will make you realize what it is?) — He Whose praise is exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ: "What, O Muḥammad, has made you know what al-Hāwiya is?"
Then He clarified what this is, saying: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ — by al-ḥāmiya (the blazing hot) is meant: that which is heated by the fuel kindled upon it.
